A world wanders through that desert of love, hoping to enter the Kaʿbah of acceptance. With the road thus filled by unmet longing and disappointment, heaven commanded again: "O Gabriel, look again." 

### In short

- Women, children, piled gold and silver, marked horses, cattle and land are made appealing as a test, not condemned as things in themselves.
- Each desire turns on intention: marriage, children, wealth and horses can serve Allah or feed pride, domination and forgetfulness.
- The safe measure is need without captivity, the boat kept on the water rather than filled with it, because with Allah is the final and perishing-free return.

15.text:
Verse 14 calls present blessings temporary, and verse 15 asks: "Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Shall I inform you of what is better than ˹all of˺ this? Those mindful ˹of Allah˺ will have Gardens with their Lord under which rivers flow, to stay there forever, and pure spouses, along with Allah’s pleasure.” And Allah is All-Seeing of ˹His˺ servants". The question expects a yes. Against six beloved things of this world, it sets gardens, purified spouses and the approval of Allah, and approval is the greatest of the three.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Shall I inform you of what is better than ˹all of˺ this?"**: the interrogative is meant as an affirmation. It asks whether people obsessed with imperfect, perishable blessings want to be told of blessings far better, prepared for those who fear Allah and obey Him.

**"Those mindful ˹of Allah˺ will have Gardens with their Lord under which rivers flow, to stay there forever"**: for those who have taqwa there are Gardens with their Lord, underneath which rivers flow, and they remain there forever and do not want removal. The rivers run throughout Paradise carrying honey, milk, wine and water, moving beneath trees and habitations, of a kind no eye has seen, no ear has heard and no heart has imagined. They will neither die nor leave.

**"and pure spouses, along with Allah’s pleasure"**: purified mates, free from filth, dirt, harm, menstruation, post-natal bleeding and every defect of form or character that belongs to this world. The pleasure of Allah is added after the gardens, and it is greater than all of them: "But the pleasure of Allah is greater" (9:72). Once it descends, Allah will never be angry with them after it.

**"And Allah is All-Seeing of ˹His˺ servants"**: Allah sees His servants, their places in Paradise and their works in the life of this world. Nothing is hidden from Him, and He gives and requites each according to what he deserves and what he did.

### Who first hears the promise

The fearful are described as those who keep away from disbelief, from ascribing partners to Allah and from indecencies, and Abū Bakr and his fellow believers are named as the first case of them. Their gardens stand with their Lord. Their pure companions are spared menses and filth. Their Lord's contentment is far greater than the bliss they enjoy, and He sees the believers both in their stations in Paradise and in their deeds here.

### Why the next world names only three blessings

Verse 14's infatuations numbered six: children and women, cattle and tillage, fine horses, and heaps of silver and gold. Verse 15 names three blessings of the Hereafter: gardens, purified wives and Allah's approval. The others are not denied, and each absence has a reason.

Children were not named because in this world a man loves children for their help and strength and because his name lives on through them. In the Hereafter he will not need such help, and he will not die and need an heir. Those who have children will have them in Paradise, and whoever has no children here will not desire them there. Should someone wish for a child, Allah will grant him one. A hadith in the Jāmiʿ of at-Tirmidhī says that if a dweller of Paradise wishes to have a child, pregnancy, birth and growth will be completed in no time, and he will have what he wished for.

Gold and silver were not named because here they buy and procure. In the next life there is nothing to buy, sell or pay for, and whatever a dweller needs is instantly provided. Paradise is not without gold and silver, since some reports describe places there built with bricks of gold and silver laid alternately, but metal is not the blessing worth naming.

Horses cover distances here, and there is no travel there of that kind, though sound hadith reports that fine horses will be brought before the dwellers of Paradise on Fridays for them to ride out to meet friends and relatives. Cattle and farms serve needs already supplied in Paradise without intermediaries. One report in aṭ-Ṭabarānī says that even a person who wishes, without need, to try farming will have everything assembled instantly, and ploughing, seeding, ripening and cutting will be done in no time.

The one named blessing of companionship then covers the rest, because Paradise holds a comprehensive promise: for its people there is whatever they wish. What is mentioned is already present without asking. What is not mentioned arrives on wishing.

### The approval that cannot be withdrawn

The last and greatest blessing is hard to picture. When the people of Paradise have settled, happy and content with no desire unfulfilled, Allah will ask whether they are happy and whether they need anything. They will answer that He has given them everything, so what else could they need. He will say that He now gives them the greatest of all blessings: His approval, with the promise that He will never be displeased with them, and nearness forever. Since displeasure cannot return, the blessings of Paradise cannot be taken back or reduced either.

The Prophet ﷺ summed up the whole subject in a hadith reported by Ibn Mājah and aṭ-Ṭabarānī from Abū Hurairah: "Worldly life is cursed and cursed is what is in there, except what is used to seek the pleasure of Allah." Another narration gives the exceptions as the remembrance of Allah, dhikr, and what Allah likes, and the religious scholar, ʿālim, and the student of religion, ṭālib ʿilm.

### The degrees of godwariness and of Paradise

The text leaves enemies at their furthest goal and returns to friends. Godwariness rises by levels, so Paradise rises by degrees. Its first degree, the Garden of the Shelter, belongs to the first godwariness, shunning what is forbidden and refusing the soul's caprice. Scripture binds them: "As for him who fears the standing..." (79:40-41). Higher stands Eden Garden, and beyond Eden stands approval at its greatest: "And goodly dwellings in the gardens of..." (9:72).

The Greatest Approval belongs to those who reach the utmost godwariness. That utmost is reached when a person treats everything carrying the scar of new arrival and the mark of creation as an enemy, as Abraham said: "Surely they are an enemy to me, ..." (26:77). Then he turns away from all things, keeps his heart detached, and busies himself with the suffering of passion for the ultimate Reality. The intrusion of others finds no room there. The heart becomes a garden with room either for the intruder or for the image of the Beloved, so it is given wholly to Him, and a whiff of union does what a hundred spirits cannot. Tomorrow all people are carried to the furthest limit of their goals. Whoever hopes for the Garden of Refuge is told to flee the unlawful and deal justly, and it will not be held back from him.

### In short

- Better than all worldly loves are Gardens with rivers, purified spouses and Allah's pleasure, and His pleasure is the greatest because it never turns to anger.
- Children, gold, silver, horses, cattle and farms are not separately promised because Paradise supplies their purposes, and whatever is wished for is given there.
- Allah sees His servants and their works, and Paradise itself is graded with godwariness, up to the Greatest Approval, which outranks even the Garden of Eden.

16.text:
The sixteenth verse gives the words of the people entitled to that promise: "who pray, “Our Lord! We have believed, so forgive our sins and protect us from the torment of the Fire.”" They are described first by a prayer, not by an achievement. Faith is confessed, sin is admitted, and protection is begged, and the two verses around this one explain why such people ask in exactly this way.

### Phrase by phrase

**"who pray"**: the verse introduces the people of Paradise by what they say in prayer. The word "those", alladhīna, here qualifies the mindful who were promised the gardens in the verse before, or stands in substitution for them, so that the prayer and the promise belong to one people.

**"Our Lord! We have believed"**: we believe in You, in Your Book and in Your Messenger, and in what You revealed to Your messengers. We have followed Your sacred law.

**"so forgive our sins"**: forgive our errors and shortcomings on the ground of faith in You and in the law You gave, out of Your bounty and mercy. The sins named cover those committed before Islam and those committed after its advent.

**"and protect us from the torment of the Fire"**: guard us and drive away from us the punishment of Hell.

### Why this prayer follows belief so closely

A person convinced that the matters of the next world are entirely in his Lord's hands finds worldly glitter meaningless. God becomes the being he fears most, and the next life the thing he wants most. He stops following mundane desire and settles his course by looking toward the court of the Almighty. Then his prayer grows natural. In solitude God is his companion. Before divine greatness and perfection his own being shrinks to insignificance, and he has hardly any words left except, "O my God, forgive me."

The prayer therefore joins two confessions. We have believed, so the relationship is real, and we have sinned, so forgiveness cannot be assumed. Forgive us our sins because of our faith in You is the order of the sentence: faith is what a servant brings, while forgiveness comes from the bounty and mercy of the Lord addressed.

### Wholly occupied, and the nearness it wins

Read inwardly, the saying of these people means that they occupy themselves with Allah entirely, bi-l-kulliyya, and plead for help before Him at the mention of severe trials and afflictions, al-raziyya. Those who pray this way obtain nearness and intimate friendship with Him, al-qurba wa-l-khuṣūṣiyya, together with high degrees, al-darajāt al-ʿuliyya, and pleasing shares, al-qisam al-murḍiyya. Their own summary is simple. In the presence of His greatness they call on Him spontaneously, and He becomes the companion of their solitude.

### In short

- The people of the promise are introduced by prayer: belief confessed, sins laid before Allah, and protection from the Fire begged.
- Forgiveness is asked for on the ground of faith, from Allah's bounty and mercy, for sins before Islam and after it.
- Read inwardly, the prayer is the mark of people wholly occupied with Allah, who receive nearness, high degrees and pleasing shares.

17.text:
The seventeenth verse completes the portrait: "˹It is they˺ who are patient, sincere, obedient, and charitable, and who pray for forgiveness before dawn". Five qualities are named, and the last one is timed. Prayer for forgiveness is placed in the final part of the night, when sleep is sweetest and no audience is present, and the whole verse looks back to the prayer of verse 16 and explains who can honestly say it.

### Phrase by phrase

**"who are patient"**: patient while performing acts of obedience and abandoning what is forbidden. The steadfast are also understood as those steady in carrying out the obligations Allah enjoined and in shunning His contraventions, and as the steadfast when misfortunes strike.

**"sincere"**: truthful in their proclamation of faith, proving it by difficult deeds. They are truthful in faith, and truthful in their words and actions too.

**"obedient"**: they submit to Allah and obey Him and His Messenger, fulfilling His sacred law completely. They are compliant before God.

**"and charitable"**: they spend from their wealth on the acts of obedience they were commanded, in kindness to kith and kin, help for the needy and comfort for the destitute. They spend in the way of Allah.

**"and who pray for forgiveness before dawn"**: they beg Allah's pardon in the last hours of the night, saying, "Lord, forgive us." That time is singled out because it is the hour of unawareness and of the joy of sleep, when hearts are least distracted and prayers are most likely to be accepted.

### What al-Muttaqīn add to the prayer

Allah calls these people al-Muttaqīn, the mindful who fear Him, and He promised them tremendous rewards. Their patience covers obedience performed and prohibitions left. Their truthfulness covers faith declared and faith acted on. Their obedience is plain submission. Their spending runs from commanded worship to the care of relatives and the poor. Their seeking of forgiveness is then set at night because that practice testifies to the virtue of asking pardon in its latter part.

A family precedent is even given. When Yaʿqūb (Jacob) told his sons, "I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you" (12:98), he waited until the latter part of the night to make the supplication.

### The last third of the night

Reports in the Two Sahihs, the Musnad and the Sunan collections agree on the Prophet's words:

> "Every night, when the last third of it remains, our Lord, the Blessed, the Superior, descends to the lowest heaven saying, 'Is there anyone to ask Me, so that I may grant him his request? Is there anyone to invoke Me, so that I may respond to his invocation? Is there anyone seeking My forgiveness, so that I may forgive him?'" 

His practice fits that hour. ʿĀʾishah, in the Two Sahihs, remembered witr offered across the night (early, middle and late), but toward the end of his life he confined it to the late part. ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar prayed by night while repeatedly asking Nāfiʿ whether the last part had arrived. Once Nāfiʿ confirmed it, supplication and seeking forgiveness continued until dawn. Ibn Abī Ḥātim collected that report.

### The five qualities, limb by limb

The five are also distributed across the person. The patient are patient with their hearts, the truthful truthful with their spirits, the devoted devoted with their souls, the expenders spend what they are able, and those who seek forgiveness at dawn do so with their tongues. Such people are the chevaliers, whose speaking and doing agree. In the heart they remain patient under the Real's command. In the spirit they walk straight in His covenant. In the body they observe the rightful due of His command. With wealth they spend on His road. With the tongue they ask forgiveness and seek from His generosity.

Neither world can detain the patient. Trial after trial is borne without complaint until the Patron is reached, with faces turned from worldly and otherworldly distractions. Truthfulness begins in speech aimed straight at the goal, continues in travel and thought, and finally drops even its visible marks. Such a person plunges onward toward security and "the seat of truthfulness, at an Omnipotent King" (54:55). The devoted grip the door, swallow sorrow, set loved ones and companions aside, and seek proximity. Poverty becomes clothing and empty hands rise at generosity's doorway: "Until You open, we will not leave, and until You caress, we will not go away." Standing alternates with prostration, hope with fear. Then comes the caress from the Exalted Presence: friendship's road is solitary, its wine's drinker is promised vision, and the truthful eventually reach desire. A longing poem waits for one glance from Allah, sorrow's end, fortune entering the door and elation's sun rising. Expenders give property as far as ability reaches, then spend selves through deeds and hearts through truthful states.

The portrait of verse 16's prayer can now be seen from the inside. God's people fear Him most, desire the next life most, and keep words and actions in agreement. Their wealth no longer belongs to them but is devoted to His cause. Hardship on His path does not turn them, because no one else can rescue a person who turns away from God. Their hearts are full of His remembrance, dhikr, and they call on Him spontaneously. The path, the remembrance and the pardon-seeking are one life, not three.

### In short

- The mindful are patient, truthful, obedient, generous, and devoted to seeking forgiveness in the last part of the night.
- That hour is honoured by the Prophet's own practice and by the promise that Allah calls out then for anyone who asks, invokes or seeks forgiveness.
- Inwardly the five qualities cover heart, spirit, body, wealth and tongue, and they make the prayer of the verse before a description of a whole life.

18.text:
The surah now returns to the Oneness with a list of witnesses: "Allah ˹Himself˺ is a Witness that there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—and so are the angels and people of knowledge. He is the Maintainer of justice. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—the Almighty, All-Wise". Allah's own testimony comes first, and Allah is sufficient as a witness. The angels and the possessors of knowledge join a testimony they did not create, and the repetition fixes the point before the question of religion is taken up in the next verse.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Allah ˹Himself˺ is a Witness that there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him"**: Lordship and godhood belong to Him alone over every created thing. All else serve Him, depend on Him and need Him, whereas He is rich beyond needing anyone. Proofs and signs have made this plain to creation. It is the greatest testimony possible, affirming Allah's sole right to worship and the perfection of justice across creation and sacred law alike. Legislative and universal signs converge on His divinity.

**"and so are the angels and people of knowledge"**: angels affirm it. So do possessors of knowledge among prophets and believers, by conviction and by speech. Angels stay near Allah and execute His instructions, testifying with knowledge and sight that He alone merits worship. Ulū al-ʿilm, people of knowledge, are first the prophets and those formed by Islam's knowledge.

**"He is the Maintainer of justice"**: Justice governs every act by which He maintains creation. The Arabic participle, qāʾiman, stands in the accusative as a circumstance, governed by an implied sense of being alone in the upholding: He alone is upholding His creatures with justice, constantly and uniquely.

**"There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—the Almighty, All-Wise"**: the statement is repeated for emphasis. The Almighty does not submit to weakness, because of His might and greatness, and cannot be overpowered, while the All-Wise is wise in His creation, planning and legislation, in all His statements, actions and decrees. Allah says the same of His own witnessing elsewhere: "But Allah bears witness to that which He has sent down (the Qur'an) unto you (O Muhammad ﷺ)" (4:166).

### The honour given to the possessors of knowledge

Al-Ghazālī found in this verse a great honour for the scholars, because Allah mentions their witness together with His own and with that of the angels. The phrase may also be taken more widely. It may mean everyone who, by inquiry on sound intellectual principles or by reflecting on this universe, reaches knowledge of the unity of Allah, even if he is not a scholar by formal training in the traditional sense. The testimony does not change in either case. It is borne by the Being whose being and attributes, and the manifestations of whose power and creativity across the world, are themselves open signs of His Oneness, and it is confirmed by His messengers and Books.

### Why two Jewish scholars asked for this verse

The verse is also called the verse of shahādah, witness. Al-Baghawī reports that two leading Jewish scholars came to Madinah from Syria. Looking at the township, they told one another that its appearance matched the prophecy in the Torah that the last of the prophets would live there. They heard that a very pious man lived there whom people called a prophet, and they went to see the Prophet ﷺ. His appearance reminded them of every attribute the Torah had predicted. They said to him, "You are Muhammad?" He said, "Yes." They said, "You are Ahmad?" He said, "Yes, I am Muhammad and Ahmad." Then they said they had one question, and if he answered it correctly they would embrace Islam. He told them to ask. They asked, "Which is the greatest witness in the Book of Allah?" This verse was revealed as the answer, he recited it to them, and both embraced Islam at once.

Reports attach promises to its recitation. In the Musnad of Aḥmad, the Prophet ﷺ recited this verse at ʿArafat and then said, "And to that, O my Lord, I too am a witness." Al-Aʿmash relates that whoever recites the verse and says those words will be addressed by Allah to the angels on the Last Day in these terms: My servant has made a promise while I am foremost in keeping a promise, so let My servant be admitted into Paradise. Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said that whoever recites Āyat al-Kursī, "Allah! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him" (2:255), the verse Shahidal-lāhu (3:18) and the verse of the kingdom up to "without measure" (3:26-27) will have all his sins forgiven, be admitted to Paradise, and have seventy needs taken care of, plenty of them, the simplest being forgiveness itself.

### The witness before there was anything to witness with

An inward reading reaches behind creation itself. Self-witness belongs to the Real: He celebrates Himself and attests His attributes fittingly, proclaiming existence, independence, self-subsistence and permanence. Back then no creature could refuse, ignore or recognise anything. Intellect had not arrived, heavens and space did not exist, and neither brightness nor shadow had appeared. Adam was absent, as were universe, air, land, sea, light and darkness. Still the Lord of the Worlds spoke in majestic measure, witnessing a unity without peer. He remains unchanged and everlasting. First and Last, Outward and Inward, He knows beings and non-beings. As Outward He dominates through compelling greatness. As Inward He escapes imaginative reasoning about "how". 

Creaturely witness therefore adds no missing support. Its gift is felicity for witnesses themselves. Angels, prophets and knowers receive astonishing eminence when Allah joins their testimony to His own. Only His exaltedness truly recognises Him and grasps His unity. Heaven, earth, both worlds, Paradise and Hell cannot measure His kingdom's permanence or divinity's perfection. "Who knows You? It is You who know You, You. No one knows You. You alone know You." He chose their felicity, set them apart, caressed them and opened recognition to them. "And God singles out for His mercy whomsoever He will" (2:105).

The universe makes the same confession in action. It is run by its Master through unseen agents, the angels, and it presents itself as one completely unitary system, which indicates a single Planner. Every part stands in a state of surrender, performing its function according to the appointed plan, and that order, in which everything is in its right place, proves that its Lord loves justice and righteousness. The surrender required of people is the same performance, now chosen.

### In short

- Allah, the angels and the possessors of knowledge witness that none deserves worship but Him, and He upholds creation in justice.
- The verse honours the scholars by joining their witness to His, though His own witness needed no support, and it answered two scholars from Syria who asked for the greatest witness in the Book.
- Before any created thing existed, the Real witnessed to the Real, and He remains the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward.

19.text:
The next verse names the religion that follows from that testimony: "Certainly, Allah’s only Way is Islam. Those who were given the Scripture did not dispute ˹among themselves˺ out of mutual envy until knowledge came to them. Whoever denies Allah’s signs, then surely Allah is swift in reckoning". The first sentence closes every other road. The second explains why the road was refused by people who had already received Scripture. The third sets the reckoning in motion.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Certainly, Allah’s only Way is Islam"**: there is no religion accepted with Allah from any person except Islam. Islam here names submission, obedience to the commands of Allah in complete surrender, believing in all the prophets of all times and in what they brought, and acting accordingly. It includes obeying all the messengers up to Muhammad ﷺ, who finalised their commission and closed all paths to Allah except through himself. The verse is also read, with anna in place of inna, as a continuation of the testimony before it: shahida Llāhu, God bears witness, anna ad-dīna ʿinda Llāhi al-islām, that religion with God is Islam.

**"Those who were given the Scripture did not dispute ˹among themselves˺ out of mutual envy until knowledge came to them"**: the Jews and Christians divided in religion, some affirming God's Oneness and others rejecting it. They did so only after Allah had sent messengers and revealed Books with the proofs that should have prevented it. The cause was transgression and baghy, resentful envy, hatred and enmity between them, in which some wronged others and some defied even those they hated when the hated were right. They split into groups and sects after evidence had been established, out of envy and greed for the world.

**"Whoever denies Allah’s signs, then surely Allah is swift in reckoning"**: whoever rejects what Allah sent down in His Book will be punished for his rejection, reckoned for his denial and tormented for defying His Book. The swiftness can be felt at once, because reckoning begins soon after death, in the state called barzakh. The detailed accounting waits for the Day of Judgment, when a person answers for his doings in the minutest detail.

### One dīn, many laws

The word dīn has several senses in Arabic, and one of them is "the way". In the Qur'an's own usage it stands for the principles and injunctions common to all prophets, from Adam to the last of them, Muhammad al-Muṣṭafā ﷺ. Subsidiary injunctions, which differed by age and community, are called sharīʿah, minhāj or, in later terms, madhhab. Allah says: "Allah made you follow the same religion with which He bound Nuh (and other prophets)" (42:13).

That shared dīn affirms Allah as perfect in Being and attributes, flawless, and alone worthy of worship, with belief held inwardly and spoken outwardly. It also affirms judgment's Day, final accounting, reward and punishment, Paradise and Hell. Every messenger sent by Him and every commandment carried by them belong inside it, again believed in heart and confessed by tongue.

At root Islam means handing oneself over to Allah in obedience. Anyone who believed his own age's prophets and obeyed Allah through them could rightly be called Muslim, with Islam as his religion. Nūḥ (Noah) said, "I have been commanded that I be from among the Muslims" (10:72). Ibrāhīm (Abraham) described himself and his community the same way: "Our Lord, make us Muslims, the submitting ones to Thee, and from our progeny a community of Muslims submitting to Thee" (2:128). The disciples of ʿĪsā said, "And bear witness that we are Muslims" (3:52). Since Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ, whoever meets Allah by a path other than his meets Him by one that will not be accepted. "And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted of him" (3:85).

In its second sense the word names the law brought finally by the last prophet, which abrogated all previous ways and stands until the Day of Judgment, and which the Prophet ﷺ explained in the well-known hadith of Jibrīl (Gabriel). Both readings end in the same place. In the age of Nūḥ, Islam was what Nūḥ brought. In the age of Ibrāhīm, what Ibrāhīm brought. In the age of Mūsā (Moses), Islam took the form of the tablets of the Torah and his teachings. In the age of ʿĪsā (Jesus), it came as the Injīl and his teachings. After the last prophet, the injunctions of earlier codes that were abrogated no longer count as Islam at all, and Islam is what took shape on the pattern given by the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

### Why good deeds outside submission do not save

These verses cut at the root of an approach that places Islam and kufr, disbelief, on one footing in the name of tolerance, and claims that every faith in the world, Judaism, Christianity or even paganism, can be a source of salvation provided its followers do good deeds and keep good morals. The material calls this a veiled attempt to empty Islam of substance and to make it something that can be moulded to fit any religion, even disbelief. Light and darkness are not the same, and it is absurd to suppose that Allah loves disobedience and rebellion as He loves obedience and submission. Whoever denies even one basic principle of Islam is, without any shadow of doubt, a rebel against Allah, however impressive his other deeds and formal morality may look. Salvation in the Hereafter depends first on obedience to Allah and His Messenger. For those who remain deprived of it, "We shall not assign weight to their deeds on the Day of Judgment" (18:105).

### Why the People of the Book disputed a prophet they recognised

After declaring the religion, the verse explains the dispute over the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ. The People of the Book did not act from doubt. Through their own Scriptures they knew the truth of the matter, but they feared losing ground to the Muslims. Malice toward Muslims, love of power and influence, and an arrogant self-image as traditional leaders drove the altercations. The exposition of what stood in their Scripture had already come to them, and the difference broke out after that knowledge, through transgression among themselves. Where the truth is refused in that way, the reckoning is swift.

### Three stations of submission

Approved religion means looking toward Allah as servants, worshipping by His decree, seeking His approval and returning to Him. Its submission has three stations. First comes public acknowledgement protecting blood and property. The speaker's neck escapes the sword and wealth remains his regardless of conformity, hypocrisy, following or innovation. Right belief, loyalty in deeds and adherence to Sunnah mark the second. Surrender crowns the path at the third station, pleasing God and sheltering recognition. It casts a person onto the Real's high threshold, approves His decree without protest or aversion, follows Him and treats His decision with reverence.

That third station is what Abraham asked for himself and Ishmael: "Our Lord, make us submitters to Thee!" (2:128). It is what he answered when it was said to him, "Submit!", and he said, "I submit to the Lord of the worlds" (2:131). And it is alluded to in the words told of Joseph: "Receive me as a submitter and join..." (12:101).

### In short

- The only religion accepted with Allah is Islam: one dīn of submission shared by every prophet, while the laws that carry it changed by age and were completed in Muhammad ﷺ.
- The People of the Book split only after knowledge came, through envy, malice and love of position, so their deeds outside submission carry no saving weight (18:105).
- Reckoning is swift: it begins in barzakh after death and is completed in detail on the Day of Judgment.

20.text:
When argument continues after recognition, the Prophet ﷺ is told what to say: "So if they argue with you ˹O Prophet˺, say, “I have submitted myself to Allah, and so have my followers.” And ask those who were given the Scripture and the illiterate ˹people˺, “Have you submitted yourselves ˹to Allah˺?” If they submit, they will be ˹rightly˺ guided. But if they turn away, then your duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺. And Allah is All-Seeing of ˹His˺ servants". The answer to the dispute is not more dispute. It is a declaration, an invitation to both audiences at once, and a limit placed on the caller's responsibility.

### Phrase by phrase

**"So if they argue with you ˹O Prophet˺, say, “I have submitted myself to Allah, and so have my followers.”"**: when Jews and Christians dispute tawḥīd, His Oneness, do not trade argument indefinitely. State the stance. My worship is purified for Allah alone, alongside no partner, rival, offspring or companion, and believers with me share that religion and creed. Literally the claim is "I have surrendered my countenance". Wajh, the face, is picked for its nobility because bodily surrender soon follows facial surrender and submission. Allah puts the same claim in the Prophet's mouth elsewhere: "Say (O Muhammad ﷺ): 'This is my way; I invite unto Allah with sure knowledge, I and whosoever follows me...'" (12:108).

**"And ask those who were given the Scripture and the illiterate ˹people˺, “Have you submitted yourselves ˹to Allah˺?”"**: say to the Jews and Christians, and to the unlettered Arab idolaters, "Have you too surrendered?", which carries the force of a command: Submit! The caller is sent to both groups at once, to the People of the two Scriptures and to the pagan Arabs, with one religion, one way and one law.

**"If they submit, they will be ˹rightly˺ guided. But if they turn away, then your duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺"**: surrender like yours brings guidance out of error. Turning away sends accounting, return and destination back to Allah. Your obligation stops at delivery.

**"And Allah is All-Seeing of ˹His˺ servants"**: He has perfect knowledge of who deserves guidance and who does not. He guides whom He wills and allows whom He wills to stray, with perfect wisdom and unequivocal proof in all of it, because "He cannot be questioned for what He does, while they will be questioned" (21:23). He sees those who believe and those who do not, and He requites His servants for their deeds. This address was given before the command to fight them was revealed.

### A message to all mankind

Similar verses plainly prove Muhammad's message reaches all creation. Allah says, "Say (O Muhammad ﷺ): 'O mankind! Verily, I am sent to you all as the Messenger of Allah'" (7:158), and "Blessed be He Who sent down the criterion to His servant that he may be a warner to the 'Alamin (mankind and Jinn)" (25:1). Hadith collections beyond the Two Sahihs also preserve reports that letters went out during his lifetime to earth's kings and assorted peoples. Arabs and non-Arabs, scriptured communities and illiterate audiences all received the summons exactly as he had been commanded.

ʿAbd ar-Razzāq recorded that Abū Hurayrah said the Prophet ﷺ declared, "By He in Whose Hand is my soul! No member of this Ummah, no Jew or Christian, hears of me but dies without believing in what I was sent with, but will be among the people of the Fire." Muslim also recorded that hadith. The Prophet ﷺ said, "I was sent to the red and the black." And he said, "A Prophet used to be sent to his people, but I was sent to all mankind."

The surah began by confirming the Divine Oneness and refuting the Trinity, and the disputations of the People of the Book have continued after the truth was proved conclusively. The advice given here is that their acceptance or rejection is no measure of the believer's own standing. A believer declares that he and those with him have entered Islam with no doubt about its truth. The mission itself was for the disputers' own good. If they submit they are rightly guided, and if they keep a hostile attitude, the Prophet ﷺ is comforted: his duty was conveying the message of Allah and His commandments, and the rest belongs to Allah, who is in full sight of what His servants do.

### How to look at people who refuse

An inward discipline hides inside delivery's command. View disputants through Allah's free disposal, taṣrīf, so their unequal stages and differences cannot unsettle your own state. Behind varied treatment stands one decisive power, qudra, assigning each person the lot He chose. Counsel publicly in public, and privately witness His disposal concerning them. Give the tongue to advice while clearing the heart of their chatter and withdrawing the inmost self from watching them. You were assigned delivery, never management of outcomes. Initiating and bringing affairs about belongs to Him.

### In short

- The answer to continued argument is a declaration: I and my followers have submitted to Allah, and the same submission is put to the People of the Scripture and the unlettered alike.
- Submission means guidance, and refusal leaves reckoning to Allah, since the Messenger's duty ends at delivering the message and this was said before the command to fight.
- The call is universal, to kings and peoples, Arabs and non-Arabs, as the letters and the hadith in Muslim affirm.

21.text:
The warning turns historical: "Indeed, those who deny Allah’s signs, kill the prophets unjustly, and kill people who stand up for justice—give them good news of a painful punishment". The phrase "good news" is sarcasm. Behind it stand the past crimes of the People of the Book, the killing of prophets who brought them nothing but the truth, and the killing of ordinary people whose offence was to enjoin justice.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, those who deny Allah’s signs"**: disbelief in Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur'an is meant, and, among the Jews, refusal of Injīl and Qur'an as well. People of the Book are rebuked for past and recent transgression, defying messengers, rejecting truth and refusing obedience.

**"kill the prophets unjustly"**: they killed many prophets when the prophets conveyed to them what Allah had legislated, without cause or criminal behaviour on the prophets' part, since the prophets only called them to truth. The word is also read yuqātilūna, "they fight against" the prophets. In one explanation the slayers are widened to those who ally themselves with the slayers of the prophets, wrongfully, when the prophets had committed no crime.

**"and kill people who stand up for justice"**: they also kill those of mankind who believed in the prophets and enjoin equity, meaning Allah's divine Oneness, and moderation in deeds and morals. This is the worst type of arrogance. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Kibr (arrogance) is refusing the truth and degrading people."

**"give them good news of a painful punishment"**: announce to them a painful and humiliating torment, a doom that will spread out to their hearts. The good tidings are sarcastic ridicule, and the fāʾ in fa-bashshirhum, "so give them good tidings" works like the answer to a condition: if they disbelieve, then give them this news.

### Forty-three prophets in one day

A report transmitted in Rūḥ al-Maʿānī from Ibn Abī Ḥātim has the Prophet ﷺ explaining this verse with a number. The Banū Isrāʾīl slew forty-three prophets at one and the same time. Then one hundred and seventy pious elders stood up to ask them to uphold justice, and they slew those too on the same day. The event is given as forbidden to them in advance: forty-three prophets killed, and a hundred and seventy devout worshippers who forbade the act, each killed immediately. That pattern, taken together, drew an answer. Rejected truth plus contempt for creatures brought disgrace and humiliation now, with humiliating torment reserved later.

### A perpetual turning away

Those bound to disappointment, khidhlān, and branded with deprivation, ḥirmān, are told that Allah's turning away from them is perpetual. He has already determined their transfer from one abode of disgrace, hawān, to another: from disappointment and deprivation to punishment and fires, nīrān. The inward logic matches the history. A true argument is also one of Allah's signs, and someone who will not bow to a true argument will not bow to God. Deniers refuse the truth not because it is unclear to them but because acknowledgement would concede the standing of the one who brings it, and jealousy and arrogance do not allow that. In the extreme, they want to exterminate the caller himself.

### In short

- The crimes named are denial of the signs, killing prophets without right, and killing those who enjoin justice, and the punishment announced as "good news" is ridicule.
- A report puts forty-three prophets and a hundred and seventy elders who forbade the killing into a single day.
- Arrogance, defined by the Prophet ﷺ as refusing truth and degrading people, is answered by disgrace here and humiliation hereafter.

22.text:
The account closes with an audit: "They are the ones whose deeds are wasted in this world and the Hereafter. And they will have no helpers". Nothing they built survives the transfer. Their works fail in both abodes, and when the punishment comes, no one steps between them and it.

### Phrase by phrase

**"They are the ones whose deeds are wasted in this world and the Hereafter"**: even charitable spending and kindness toward relatives count as failed and invalid across both worlds. Nothing remains on their ledger, because such deeds lack consequence without faith. People guilty of denial, killing and injustice gain no benefit here and receive no reward later.

**"And they will have no helpers"**: no protectors from the chastisement, and no one who will save them from Allah's punishment.

### Why the works failed

The failure is measured in two currencies. Today they are granted no success in their works, tawfīq bi-aʿmāl. Tomorrow their hopes go unrealised, taḥqīq li-āmāl. That is because they lost Allah's help in both abodes and did not bear witness to His might and power. The plans such people lay against the callers of truth, to censor their words and silence them, fail in the same way. When the scales of justice are set up, the actions that had convinced them of success and salvation turn out to have no value at all. They will enter the next world divested of all support.

### In short

- Charity and kindness to kin cannot rescue deeds built on denial and murder, so their works are wasted here and hereafter.
- No helper will protect them from the punishment.
- The loss is twinned: no success granted to their works today, and no hopes realised tomorrow.

23.text:
The verse asks, "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scriptures? Yet when they are invited to the Book of Allah to settle their disputes, some of them turn away heedlessly". They claim to follow the Torah and the Injīl, yet when they are called to refer to those books, with what Allah commanded them about following Muhammad ﷺ inside them, a party turns away with aversion. The censure falls on defiance, and three different occasions are given for the call they refused.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scriptures?"**: the Jews addressed already possessed Torah knowledge testifying to Muhammad's prophethood. Their share, a mere portion of the Book, had reached them.

**"Yet when they are invited to the Book of Allah to settle their disputes"**: they are called to the Book of Allah so that it may judge between them in what they differ about. The verb "being called" marks their state at the moment of refusal.

**"some of them turn away heedlessly"**: a party of them turned away, opposed to accepting its rulings, ignoring the judgement because it did not agree with their desires. People who claim to follow the Torah ought to have accepted the Torah's own judgement without hesitation.

### The stoning case at Khaybar

One occasion named is the rejection of stoning by Banū Qurayẓah and Banū al-Naḍīr among the people of Khaybar. They had been given knowledge of what stands in the Torah about stoning and other matters, and they invoked the Scripture of Allah, the Qur'an, to judge between them about stoning the married man and the married woman who had committed adultery at Khaybar, as their own Scripture prescribes. Then a faction from Banū Qurayẓah and the people of Khaybar turned away from the judgement and denied it.

The case is filled out a step further. Two Jews fornicated, and the Jews asked the Prophet ﷺ to adjudicate. He ruled that they be stoned, and they refused. The Torah was brought and consulted, and the same verdict was found in it, so the two were stoned, and the Jews became wrathful. Al-Kalbī put the occasion the same way, as the ruling on fornication at Khaybar about which the Jews asked the Prophet ﷺ, with the fuller account deferred to Surah al-Ma'idah.

### Two more occasions of the same refusal

As-Suddī reports an exchange after the call to Islam. Al-Nuʿmān ibn Awfā proposed rabbis as arbiters. The Prophet ﷺ chose Allah's Scripture instead, and the offer was rejected. Then revelation followed.

Ibn ʿAbbās gave a classroom scene through Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrimah. Inside a Jewish study house, the Prophet ﷺ invited its occupants to Allah. Nuʿaym ibn ʿAmr joined al-Ḥārith ibn Zayd in asking his religion. He answered, "The religion of Abraham." They claimed Abraham as a Jew. "Then let Torah judge between us," he replied. Refusal again brought revelation.

### A call made to people known not to answer

Inwardly the caller is being tested. You must summon people whose refusal We already know. Remain patient under the command and understand their unfortunate condition. Deprived beforehand by Our will, irāda, of beautiful self-disclosure, ḥusn al-tajallī, they become ahl al-tawallī, a people defined by turning from response, ijāba.

The refusal is puzzling on the surface, because recognition should have been easy. Allah's guidance is one and the same as what He gave various prophets at various times in various languages, and the same guidance came to the Final Prophet in the form of the Qur'an. The Qur'an's only difference from the former scriptures lies in having purified God's religion of human interpolations. People who already believe in revealed scriptures should find this call familiar. Those who deny it do so because the call does not seem serious beside their own self-styled concepts, by which they feel protected from the fire of Hell. Even if they fail to recognise the truth, they think, their salvation is not at risk. When the divine scales are set in place, they will learn how deluded that wishful thinking was.

### In short

- People given a share of the Book refused the Book's own judgement in the stoning case at Khaybar, refused the Torah as judge over the religion of Ibrāhīm (Abraham), and refused any judge but their rabbis.
- The refusal came from scholars and leaders who claimed to follow the Torah, and it fell because the judgement did not agree with their desires.
- The caller is told to be patient with people who were always going to turn away.

24.text:
The verse gives the reason in their own words: "This is because they say, “The Fire will not touch us except for a few days.” They have been deceived in their faith by their wishful lying". What made them bold enough to challenge and defy the truth was a doctrine they invented for themselves, that punishment would be short, measured and over. The verse names the doctrine a lie, and calls it the thing that deceived them in their religion.

### Phrase by phrase

**"This is because they say, “The Fire will not touch us except for a few days.”"**: the turning away and rejection happened because they said the Fire would not touch them in the Hereafter except for a certain number of days. They thought the fire of Hell would touch them only briefly, after which they would be forgiven and enter Paradise.

**"They have been deceived in their faith by their wishful lying"**: the lies they used to invent deluded them in their religion. The self-deception kept them on a false creed: they believed the Fire would touch them for a few days for their errors, but they had invented the notion themselves, and Allah gave them no authority to support the claim.

### How the few days were counted

Two counts are given, and they do not agree. One group held that they would be punished for seven days, days of the Hereafter, each day equalling a thousand years of this life, as punishment for the days in which their forefathers worshipped the calf. That makes the few days a direct measure: a thousand years of earthly reckoning for each day of fire. Allah had already exposed the same claim in Surah Al-Baqarah.

The other count makes it forty days. They contended that their forefathers had worshipped the calf for forty days, so punishment, if any, would run for the same period only, forty days, after which it would end. The deception is also explained as a claim that punishment would simply be postponed, and as a firm adherence to their religion, Judaism, held as a guarantee.

Behind both counts stood other forged securities. Self-deception was fed by the belief that they were the progeny of prophets and would therefore escape the fire of Hell altogether. Whatever form the guarantee took, the Fire was made small, and a small fire could be risked.

### Being drawn on by degrees

Inwardly the warning sharpens further. In this world they were drawn onward gradually, istidrāj, until deciding salvation and a reduced punishment for themselves felt legitimate. What passes for understanding is only falsehood. Error mistakes its own pronouncement for a binding determination, ḥukm. The doubled affliction will eventually expose it.

The blindness has a history in this surah too. The Qur'an's call did not arrive as an alien voice. The same guidance had been given to prophets before, and the Qur'an only cleared God's religion of human additions. A person carrying the earlier scriptures should recognise the call quickly. The obstacle is the private concept of safety each person has built for himself. Viewed from inside that concept, denying the truth carries no danger, because the fire has already been shortened by decree. The scales of the next world are what expose the mistake.

### In short

- The Fire was said to touch them only seven days measured at a thousand years each, or forty days matching the worship of the calf, and neither count came from Allah.
- The invented shortness of punishment made denial safe in their own eyes, which is the deception the verse names.
- Being left to build on the lie is itself a punishment, drawn on by degrees until the affliction is doubled.

25.text:
Then the shortened fire meets its Day: "But how ˹horrible˺ will it be when We gather them together on the Day about which there is no doubt—when every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and none will be wronged". The opening question looks past denial to consequence. What state awaits people who lied against Allah, rejected messengers, murdered prophets and killed scholars devoted to righteousness and resistance to evil? Allah will interrogate them about every part.

### Phrase by phrase

**"But how ˹horrible˺ will it be when We gather them together"**: how will they act, and what will their state be, when We bring them all together after they die. What will their predicament be, and how much will they regret?

**"on the Day about which there is no doubt"**: the Day of Resurrection, which will certainly come. There is no uncertainty in it.

**"when every soul will be paid in full for what it has done"**: every soul, righteous or sinner, from the People of the Scripture and from others, will receive the requital of what it earned, of good or of evil.

**"and none will be wronged"**: no good deed will be diminished and no evil deed increased. There is no oppression by reduction of good actions or addition to evil ones.

### The grandeur of that gathering

The address is called remarkable for the intensity and grandeur it conveys. Perplexity will seize the intellects of deniers. Inmost selves will reel, pretensions will be severed and hearts pulled from concealment while souls climb toward collarbones. Waiting beyond that shock stand accounting and censure, al-ḥisāb wa-l-ʿitāb, torment and punishment, al-ʿadhāb wa-l-ʿiqāb, with neither honour nor approval granted, ʿadam al-ikrām wa-l-ījāb.

There is a second resurrection set beside this one. For disbelievers, resurrection waits until Gathering Day. Lovers, by contrast, begin rising in the present moment. To explain that fully would take too long, but the contrast fixes the verse. For one company the gathering is entirely future and entirely dreadful. For another, its first rising has already begun in life.

### In short

- On a Day with no doubt in it, every soul is paid exactly what it earned, with no good diminished and no evil added.
- The gathering strips away the invented guarantees of the last verse and replaces them with reckoning and censure.
- The lovers have a resurrection that begins in the present moment, but for those who turned away the gathering is dread alone.

26.text:
The Prophet ﷺ is taught a prayer that answers every boast about power: "Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O Allah! Lord over all authorities! You give authority to whoever You please and remove it from who You please; You honour whoever You please and disgrace who You please—all good is in Your Hands. Surely You ˹alone˺ are Most Capable of everything.”" The verse was revealed while believers were digging a trench on empty stomachs and being mocked for imagining empires, and it opens with a command to praise, thank, rely and trust.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O Allah! Lord over all authorities!"**: say this while praising your Lord, thanking Him, relying on Him in all matters and trusting in Him. All sovereignty is Yours. Allāhumma means "O God", yā Allāh, the final mīm standing in place of the vocative particle yā.

**"You give authority to whoever You please and remove it from who You please"**: You are the Giver and You are the Taker. Your will is what occurs, and whatever You do not will does not occur. You decide concerning Your creation and do as You will.

**"You honour whoever You please and disgrace who You please"**: You exalt whom You will and abase whom You will, by giving the kingdom or by seizing it, according to His wisdom and justice.

**"all good is in Your Hands. Surely You ˹alone˺ are Most Capable of everything"**: in Your hand and power is good, and exaltation, abasement, sovereignty, spoils, triumph and power are all within that power. He is able to do all things, in every one of those fields.

### Gratitude for a transfer of history

Gratitude is the verse's first lesson for Messenger and ummah alike. Prophethood moved away from the Children of Israel toward an unlettered Arab of Quraysh from Makkah, the final messenger to humans and jinn. He received earlier prophets' finest qualities plus knowledge of Allah, His law, history and the Hereafter beyond any predecessor's endowment. Through his community, moreover, faith would span the world's eastern and western reaches, with his religion and law dominating older laws and faiths.

It also refutes those who thought they could decide matters for Allah. "And they say: 'Why is not this Qur'an sent down to some great man of the two towns (Makkah and Ta'if)?'" (43:31). Allah refuted them: "Is it they who would portion out the Mercy of your Lord?" (43:32), which means that Allah decides for His creation what He wills, without resistance or hindrance from anyone. He has perfect wisdom and unequivocal proof in it, and He gives prophethood to whom He wills. "Allah knows best with whom to place His Message" (6:124). "See how We prefer one above another (in this world)" (17:21).

### The trench, the rock and the three lights

The background is the battle of the Confederates, al-Ahzab, called the Trench, Khandaq. The disbelievers of Makkah had suffered repeated defeat at Badr and failure at Uhud, and Muslims were growing stronger. Disbelievers of Arabia, Jews and Christians joined in a united front to attack Madinah in a conclusive battle aimed at eradicating Islam and Muslims. The Prophet ﷺ decided in consultation with his Companions to dig a trench around parts of Madinah to block an unhindered attack.

Narrations in al-Baihaqi, Abu Nu'aim and Ibn Khuzaimah say the digging was allotted in stretches of forty hand-spans to groups of ten men. The trench ran several miles and was fairly deep and wide, so the enemy could not cross it, and it had to be finished in the shortest time. The Companions worked non-stop on hungry stomachs, finding it hard to leave even for pressing needs. The Prophet ﷺ took part in the digging like everybody else. In one stretch the diggers struck a huge rock they could not break, and they sent Salman al-Farisi to report it and ask for instructions. A named work party anchors the same episode: Salmān, Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān, al-Nuʿmān ibn Muqarrin al-Muzānī, ʿAmd ibn ʿAwf and six Helpers shared forty cubits. Flint defeated their steel and would not break.

The Prophet ﷺ came to the spot, took the pickaxe in his hands and struck. The rock shattered into pieces, and from it rose a streak of light that lit the area far and wide. He said, "In this light, I see the palaces and buildings of Hirah in the country of Persia." He struck again and a second beam rose: "In this light, I was shown the red palaces and buildings of the Byzantinians." At the third strike, "In this I was shown the great palaces of San'a in Yemen." Then he said, "I share the good news given by Jibra'il with you that my community of Muslims will prevail over all these countries."

The hypocrites of Madinah ridiculed what they heard. Here were people scared of the enemy, digging trenches without food or rest, unsure of their own lives, yet dreaming of running over Persia, the Byzantine empire and Yemen. A conquest-of-Mecca setting is also reported by Ibn ʿAbbās and Anas ibn Malik. Following the city, Muhammad ﷺ promised Persia and Byzantium to his nation. Hypocrites and Jews scoffed at the distance between aspiration and power, asking how Mecca and Medina could possibly lead to such mighty kingdoms. Qatādah adds that the Prophet ﷺ had requested those kingdoms for his nation. Other settings place ʿAbdullāh Ibn Ubayy Ibn Salūl questioning sovereignty after Mecca fell, or Quraysh challenging a prophet to match Persia's silk-couched king with visible dominion.

Appearing as a prayer, the verse turns this back on the mockers. Perfect power is displayed in the rise and fall of nations, and the verse hints that the prophecy will come to pass and Persia and the Byzantine lands will fall to Muslims. The enemies had never learned the lesson of earlier wielders of power. They judged events from the material angle, while all power and government sits in the hand of Allah, with whom lie honour and disgrace. He is not prevented from seating the poor and meek on thrones or wresting power from kings, so it should not be difficult for Him to choose ragged believers digging trenches to rule Persia, Syria, Iraq and Yemen. In the direct reading, sovereignty goes to Muhammad ﷺ and his followers and is withdrawn from the people of Persia and Byzantium, Muhammad ﷺ is exalted, and ʿAbdullāh Ibn Ubayy Ibn Salūl, Persia and Byzantium are abased.

### Why the verse names good and not evil

After giving and taking, honouring and disgracing, the text says only that good is in His hand. One might expect evil, sharr, to be paired with it, but the choice points to something real. A calamity for one person or nation may be unwelcome to them and yet, from the wider angle of the whole community of nations, not be evil at all. The Arab poet al-Mutanabbī put it briefly: the calamities of one group are the gains of another. Looked at from its relation to the Creator of the universe and in the perspective of the totality of experience, nothing is really evil in itself. In the wisdom, power and consideration of the created universe as a whole, everything can be called khair, good, as the verse puts it.

### How the Real teaches praise

Allāhumma itself teaches praise. Describe Me, says the sense, with the exaltation due to Me: Master of the kingdom. No essence partner, kingdom sharer, creating competitor, helper or companion stands beside You, so your kingship becomes known. Human kings expect humility from subjects. Seized earthly kingdoms belonged to people arrogant toward Him. Before the Real, self-abasement or tadhallul beautifies creatures, tajammul. Effacing themselves in Him, maḥw, supplies honour and might, ʿizz, while surviving in Him through annihilation, fanāʾ, supplies their remaining, baqāʾ.

Then exaltation and abasement unfold in pairs. Forsaking abases, while Your essential might exalts. Guidance into witnessing You and declaring Your oneness (tawḥīd) exalts. Denial and deprivation abase. Nearness brings good fortune, while estrangement follows turning away. Intimacy lifts one person whereas distraction from You lowers another. Exaltation can erase the lower self's controlling elements, just as abasement surrenders someone to its clamour. Intimacy sends out gleaming risings, Ṭawāliʿ, while the lower self sends night visitors, Ṭawāriq. Expansion through You, basṭ, contrasts with constriction away from You, qabḍ.

### In short

- Sovereignty is given and torn away, honour granted and disgrace imposed, all by Allah, who cannot be resisted (43:31-32, 6:124, 17:21).
- At the Trench the Prophet ﷺ split a rock and saw Hirah, the red palaces of the Byzantines and Sanʿa in three lights, and hypocrites who laughed at hungry men digging were answered with this prayer.
- "Good is in Your hand" because what ruins one nation can be another's gain, and nothing, seen whole, falls outside His good disposal.

27.text:
The prayer moves from thrones to the sky: "You cause the night to pass into the day and the day into the night. You bring forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living. And You provide for whoever You will without limit.”" The same hand that gives kingdoms lengthens and shortens every day of the year, takes life out of lifeless things and lifeless things out of life, and sets provision where no calculation can follow it.

### Phrase by phrase

**"You cause the night to pass into the day and the day into the night"**: lengths are transferred between darkness and light until balance is reached, then transferred again until one dominates. Seasons (spring, summer, autumn and winter) enact the exchange year-round. Sun and moon, indeed all spaces and heavenly bodies, operate by His command.

**"You bring forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living"**: plant yields seed and seed yields plant. Egg produces chicken and chicken produces egg. Date and date-stone exchange places, and believer and disbeliever can each emerge from the other.

**"And You provide for whoever You will without limit.”"**: You give whomever You will innumerable wealth and provision while depriving others, in wisdom and justice. Provision is given without reckoning, without straitness or inconvenience, and in abundance to whomever He chooses.

### The wider meanings of living and dead

Examples multiply in both directions. Eggs arise from birds and beasts, sperm arises from people, and fruit and dried grains arise from trees and plants. Opposite them, sperm can become a human infant, an egg a chick and a seed a tree. A living chicken may emerge from a dead egg while a dead grain leaves a living spike.

Broadly, life and death also contrast scholar with ignorant, complete with imperfect, and Muslim believer with kāfir disbeliever. Absolute power governs spiritual changes alongside physical ones. A staunch disbeliever can become a perfect believer, an ignorant person a scholar and a kāfir a Muslim. Reversal also occurs: believers can slide into disbelief while rustic people rise into learning. Ibrāhīm (Abraham) came from an idol-worshipper, but the son of Nūḥ (Noah) stayed unbelieving. Literacy does not run predictably either, since scholars, ʿālim, may father illiterate sons and illiterate men scholarly sons. The demonstration descends deliberately from cosmos to human soul.

### The provision that comes without measure

In the vaster universe Allah performs the alternation of darkness and light daily and on a colossal scale, bringing life from dead elements and causing living things to die. Nothing would be surprising if the same power appeared among human beings. Honour and power also lie in His hand. Those treated as insignificant by the leaders of the age can be raised to the highest eminence, but only those who regard such gifts as purely His gifts deserve them. The most undeserving are those who treat rank as their own acquisition.

A truth-preacher can lose home and livelihood yet remain directly guarded by Allah and specially sustained. Ordinary provision tracks effort. A messenger of truth receives without measure.

### The merit attached to these two verses

Al-Baghawī transmits a promise attached to a prescribed recitation combining Sūrat al-Fātihah, Āyat al-Kursī, the witness verse (3:18) and this pair on sovereignty (26-27). Whoever recites them receives Paradise as an abode, a place in the Sacred Enclosure, mercy seventy times daily, seventy needs fulfilled, safety from envier and enemy, and prevailing over both. Witness and sovereignty are paired because both rest on disposal belonging to Allah alone.

### Night, day and the states of the heart

Cosmic alternation maps onto the heart. Night yields to day when tawḥīd's light takes authority and erases the lower self's dark traces. Day sinks into night when hearts' suns seem eclipsed and morning indefinitely delayed. Life leaves death when listlessness vanishes, union's pledge recovers youth and heartfelt promises freshen. Death leaves life when discontent's tree sprouts thorns, hopeless people find no goodness or fragrance, and eyes and hearts fall into the confusion named in "just as they did not believe in it the first time" (6:110).

Provision beyond reckoning spares labour, kadd, exertion, jahd, a sweating brow, jabīn, and a toiling right hand, yamīn. Night becomes repose and refreshment, rāḥa, and daylight becomes delight and joy, bahja. Special gifts, karāmāt, fill the hours, while moments become approaches, qurubāt. Tongue, lisān, cannot inventory the favours, nor explanation, bayān, sound their depth. Kingship receives its closing lesson here. Anyone convinced he owns a kingdom wakes rudely when told that Allah seizes kingdoms at will, sees extinction threatening his rule and learns that self-abasement preserves it better than pompous delusion. In the truest sense a king is undistracted from witnessing the real King.

### In short

- Night and day exchange their lengths through the seasons, life and death exchange places in seed, egg, sperm and grain, and provision falls without measure.
- Living and dead also mean scholar and ignorant, believer and disbeliever: Allah brought Ibrāhīm out of an idol-worshipper and left the son of Nūḥ in unbelief.
- A hadith joins this verse to the witness verse of 3:18 with promises of Paradise, mercy seventy times a day, and protection from envier and enemy.

28.text:
The verse orders a boundary of loyalty: "Believers should not take disbelievers as guardians instead of the believers—and whoever does so will have nothing to hope for from Allah—unless it is a precaution against their tyranny. And Allah warns you about Himself. And to Allah is the final return". What is forbidden is not every dealing with non-Muslims. It is taking them as intimate guardians in place of believers, and the material separates that act carefully from kindness, courtesy and trade.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Believers should not take disbelievers as guardians instead of the believers"**: believers are prohibited from becoming supporters of disbelievers or taking them as comrades with whom they build friendship, rather than the believers. In the situation pictured, the people sought as friends were the hypocrites, ʿAbdullāh Ibn Ubayy and his companions, together with the Jews, taken in a search for might and honour in preference to sincere believers.

**"and whoever does so will have nothing to hope for from Allah"**: whoever commits what Allah prohibited in this will be discarded by Him. He has no connection with Allah, no honour, mercy or protection from Him, and does not belong to the religion of God in any way.

**"unless it is a precaution against their tyranny"**: except believers who in some places or times fear for their safety from disbelievers. Such people may save themselves by speaking toward disbelievers in a friendly way while their hearts dislike it. The word for the safeguard, tuqātan, is the verbal noun of taqiyyah, and the allowance is outward only, never inward. It was stated before the hegemony of Islam, and it applies to a person living in a land where he has no say.

**"And Allah warns you about Himself. And to Allah is the final return"**: anger and severe torment await supporters of His enemies and enemies of His friends. Warning plants fear of wrath for patronage. After death the journey ends with Him, where deeds receive reward or punishment.

### The same prohibition across the Qur'an

Allah states the ban in a series of forms. "O you who believe! Take not My enemies and your enemies as friends, showing affection towards them", ending with the words that whoever of you does that has gone astray from the straight path (60:1). "O you who believe! Take not for friends disbelievers instead of believers. Do you wish to offer Allah a manifest proof against yourselves?" (4:144). "O you who believe! Take not the Jews and the Christians as friends, they are but friends of each other. And whoever befriends them, then surely, he is one of them" (5:51). After the faithful believers are shown supporting the faithful among the Muhājirīn, the Anṣār and the Bedouins, the other side is matched against them: "And those who disbelieve are allies of one another, (and) if you do not behave the same, there will be Fitnah and oppression on the earth, and a great mischief and corruption" (8:73).

Al-Bukhārī recorded that Abū ad-Dardāʾ said, "We smile in the face of some people although our hearts curse them." Al-Bukhārī also transmitted that al-Ḥasan said, "The Tuqyah is allowed until the Day of Resurrection." The warning that follows the exception is then explained in concrete terms as a warning about unlawful killing, unlawful sex, unlawful property, intoxicants, false testimony and associating partners with Allah, the whole field of disobedience that patronage could drag a person into.

### Four degrees of relation with non-Muslims

The verses on this subject come in many places with varying shades, so the discussion collects them and distinguishes degrees. Any emotionally involved friendship from the heart is absolutely forbidden, ḥarām, while formal friendship at the level of mutual dealings is permissible, though not favoured when unnecessary.

1. **Muwālāt, close friendship.** The first degree comes from the heart: affection and love with intense emotional commitment. This kind is restricted to true Muslims, and a Muslim is not permitted it with a non-Muslim.

2. **Muwāsāt, sympathetic concern.** The second degree is sympathy, kindness and concern: charitable help and support, condolence and consolation, and any well-meaning wish for another's good. Except for disbelievers at war with Muslims, this is permissible with all other non-Muslims. Its detailed rule is given in Sūrat al-Mumtaḥinah: "Allah does not forbid you from treating those who do not fight you on your faith, nor have they driven you out of your homes, with benevolence and equity" (60:8).

3. **Mudārāt, cordial conduct.** Level three covers ordinary courtesy: pleasant manners, friendly behaviour and polite adequacy. Non-Muslims may receive it broadly, particularly to communicate faith, host guests or avert possible harm. Because cordiality can resemble close friendship, the verse's guard-yourself exception concerns this level and exempts it from prohibited intimacy.

4. **Muʿāmalāt, dealings.** The fourth degree is transactions in business, employment, wages, industry and technology. These are permissible with non-Muslims except when they harm the general body of Muslims. The continuing practice of the Prophet ﷺ, the rightly-guided caliphs and other Companions proves it. Muslim jurists accordingly prohibited selling arms to disbelievers at war with Muslims, while trade and allied activities are permitted, as is employing non-Muslims or being employed in their institutions.

The conduct of the Prophet ﷺ fills the permitted degrees with examples. When Makkah was gripped by famine he personally went out to help enemies who had driven him from his home town. At the conquest of Makkah, with all those enemies under his power, he set them free, saying there would be amnesty that day and not even censure for past tyranny. Non-Muslim prisoners of war were treated with a tenderness many people cannot claim even toward their children. Disbelievers inflicted injuries and pain on him, yet he never raised his hand in revenge and did not even wish them ill. A delegation of Banū Thaqīf, who had not yet embraced Islam, was honoured with lodging in the Prophet's mosque, the most honourable place for Muslims. ʿUmar gave stipends and allowances to needy non-Muslim dhimmīs, and the accounts of the rightly-guided caliphs and Companions are full of similar conduct. Another verse states the limit from the other side: "You shall not find those who believe in Allah and in the Hereafter having friendship with those who have enmity with Allah and His messenger, even though they may be their fathers or sons or brothers or members of their tribe" (58:22). All of the merciful treatment falls under concern, cordiality or dealings. None of it is the close and intimate friendship that is forbidden.

### Why the close bond is blocked

Life has a purpose, unlike the purposeless cycle of an animal or jungle tree that sprouts, flourishes and dies. A central aim orders every phase: eating, drinking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, living and dying. Conformity makes action sound; opposition corrupts it. For Rūmī, remembering and serving the Creator defines life, and devotion's absence makes it shameful. Lose the aim and crowds resemble humans only as empty shells. Believers declare the aim solemnly: "My prayer and my sacrifice and my life and my death are all for Allah, the Lord of the Worlds" (6:162).

Everything else then follows the purpose, including business, government, politics and personal and social relations. Those who oppose the purpose are man's worst enemies, and Satan stands foremost: "Surely, Satan is your enemy, so take him as enemy" (35:6). People who follow Satan's allurements and oppose Allah's injunctions cannot be owed deep love and intimate friendship, because a person with a definite purpose makes all friendships and enmities, agreements and disagreements, serve that purpose. The Prophet ﷺ said in a hadith in al-Bukhārī and Muslim, "Whoever loves for the sake of Allah, and hates for the sake of Allah alone, has perfected his faith." Faith, īmān, stays incomplete until love, friendship, hatred and enmity are subordinated to Allah. Deep emotional commitment therefore belongs to whoever pursues the same purpose and obeys the same Lord.

### The friendship of Allah and its reliable handhold

Faith completed sends the traveller on tawḥīd's path back into God's friendship. Friendship means alignment: loving His friends and opposing His enemies. The master of the sharīʿah called love in God and hate in God faith's most reliable handhold. One report says Allah revealed to an earlier prophet a searching question for servants who renounced the world for comfort and worshipped for reputation:

> "In this world you have taken up renunciation in order to hurry to your own comfort and be relieved of this world's suffering. With your obedience and worship you have sought your own exaltation and your own good name. Now look: What have you done for Me? Have you ever loved My friends? Have you ever taken My enemies as your enemies?"

A parallel address to Jesus says:

> "O Jesus, if the worship of all the inhabitants of heaven and earth accompanies you in the path of the religion, but you have no love for My friends and no enmity for My enemies, then your worship has been useless and without profit."

Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī told Muʿādh of loving him in God's path. Muʿādh answered with a joyful report he had heard about Resurrection Day: seats encircle the Splendorous Throne for faces shining like full moons. Terror surrounds everyone else, while these people remain secure and still. They are simply those who love one another in God. Another saying makes Allah's love obligatory for people who love, gather, visit and spend for one another in Him. Mujāhid added that when God's friends exchange smiles, sins drop like leaves from a tree.

### In short

- Believers may not take disbelievers as intimate guardians in place of believers, though outward friendliness under real fear is allowed while the heart refuses (60:1, 4:144, 5:51, 8:73).
- Kindness, courtesy and trade with non-Muslims are degrees below close friendship and are permitted, as the Prophet's famine relief, amnesty at Makkah and stipends for dhimmīs show.
- The blocked bond is the heart's, because life has one purpose (6:162), and perfected faith loves and hates for Allah's sake alone.

29.text:
The safeguard of the heart is hidden, so the next verse exposes it to view: "Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, it is known to Allah. For He knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is Most Capable of everything.”" Close friendship belongs to the heart, and no one knows the affairs of the heart but Allah, so a person who loves disbelievers inwardly while denying it verbally has no workable denial before Him.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, it is known to Allah"**: patronage hidden in breasts, inside hearts, still registers with God if disclosed outwardly or nursed privately. Hearts harbouring Muhammad's hatred, and conduct revealing it through abuse, defamation or warfare, are both recorded and requited. The verse addressed hypocrites and Jews, including the forbidden friendship they concealed.

**"For He knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth"**: He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, of good and evil, of what is secret and what is revealed.

**"And Allah is Most Capable of everything.”"**: His ability encompasses everything, including punishing those who patronise the disbelievers, regarding the dwellers of the heavens and the dwellers of the earth alike. Nothing reaches outside His power.

### Why an all-knowing God makes servants careful

Allah tells His servants that He knows the secret and apparent matters and that nothing about them escapes His observation. His knowledge encompasses them in all conditions, times, days and instances, and it encompasses everything in heaven and earth, leaving not even an atom's weight, or anything smaller, in earth, seas or mountains unobserved. Since He has perfect knowledge of everything they do and is able to punish promptly, the verse alerts servants to fear Him enough not to commit what He prohibits and dislikes. He gives respite to some people, and then He punishes them, swift and mighty in taking account.
